assertions.name: molien_is_the_unique_normalised_candidate
assertions.source: Of the three numerators present in the corpus, ONLY f^lam*q^{-kappa}*d_q sums to exactly 1 over [n]_q! at every n=1..8 in exact rational arithmetic at q=7/5. (f^lam)^2 gives n!/[n]_q!; d_q^2 is the historical unnormalised form.

assertions.name: kappa_exponent_is_forced_up_to_conjugation
assertions.source: Over c in [-3,3], the exponents making f^lam*q^{c*kappa}*d_q a measure are exactly [-1, 1] -- and those two are the same measure on transposed diagrams (conjugation invariances verified over all partitions of n<=9). So q^{-kappa} is forced up to a known symmetry, not chosen: no other exponent normalises at all. NOTE I predicted a unique exponent; the measurement says two, and the second is the rows-vs-columns duality arriving from a different direction than in qou-j7ef.

assertions.name: normalisation_is_not_a_sample_point_artifact
assertions.source: (1,1) sums to exactly 1 at a second unrelated rational q=13/4 (n=1..8) and to 1 within 1e-40 at the substrate q0 (n=3,6,9,12)

description: Bean qou-oots. Asks which q-deformation of the classical Plancherel measure (f^lam)^2/n! is normalised BY AN IDENTITY rather than by division. Of the three numerators present in this corpus, only f^lam*q^{-kappa}*d_q sums to 1 over [n]_q! -- and the kappa exponent is FORCED UP TO CONJUGATION: over c in [-3,3], exactly c = -1 and c = +1 make f^lam*q^{c*kappa}*d_q a measure, and those two are one measure read on transposed diagrams (conjugation fixes f^lam and the hook multiset and negates kappa -- verified over all partitions of n<=9), which is the same rows-vs-columns duality qou-j7ef needed. No other exponent normalises at all. Independent arithmetic confirmation of the qou-j7ef result that the Q = q^2 substitution forces the same exponent. That weight is the Molien/fake-degree family and, by that bridge, the literature's q-Plancherel measure M_{n,Q}. The historical d_q^2/[n]_q! form is NOT normalised, and the surviving alternative d_q^2/D^2 is that same numerator rescaled by whatever makes the sum 1. THIS IS A DISCRIMINATOR ON GROUNDING, NOT A DERIVED REQUIREMENT: nothing in the R1-R3 requirement set forces a family to be normalised by a theorem rather than by division, and both survivors are legitimate probability measures. Recorded as evidence for a recommendation, not as a proof of one.

T1_exact_sums_at_q_7_over_5.note: Exact Fraction arithmetic; each entry is SUM_lam numerator/[n]_q! at that n. A value of exactly 1 is an identity at this q, not an agreement to a tolerance.

T1b_kappa_exponent_family.note: w_c(lam) = f^lam * q^{c*kappa_lam} * d_q(lam) / [n]_q!, exact rational arithmetic at q=7/5, n=1..7. Only the c whose whole row is 1 gives a probability measure.

T1b_why_two_survive.explanation: f^{lam'} = f^lam, hooks(lam') = hooks(lam) as multisets, and kappa(lam') = -kappa(lam) -- all verified over every partition of n <= 9. So lam -> lam' is a bijection carrying the c=+1 summand to the c=-1 summand term by term: the two normalising exponents are one measure read on transposed diagrams, the same rows-vs-columns duality qou-j7ef needed to use Feray-Meliot's q<1 theorems at the substrate's q>1.

T3_how_far_the_others_are.note: At the substrate q0. The (0,2) column is the historical d_q^2/[n]_q! form and reproduces the figures already recorded in the corpus; the (2,0) column is n!/[n]_q!, which decreases in n where (0,2) increases -- they fail in OPPOSITE directions, so no single rescaling repairs both.
